respondents/State in RFA No. 446 of 2015 and for the appellant in RFA No. 350 of 2016.
_______________________________________________________ Satyen Vaidya,
Judge Both these appeals arise from common award passed by learned 28.08.2015, in Land Reference r District Judge, Shimla, No. 20-S/4 of 2013, on therefore, these appeals are being decided by a common judgment.
2.

The State of Himachal Pradesh issued notification dated 21.07.2015, under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, showing its intent to acquire land for construction of Dhadu Ghai Nerwa Rinjet Diyandli road.

The land of the appellants in RFA No. 446 of 2015 (hereinafter referred to as claimants), measuring 0-08-11 Hectares comprised in Khasra No. 72, situated in village Diyandli,
Sub-Tehsil Nerwa, District Shimla, H.P., was also included in aforesaid notification and was eventually acquired.

3. The Land Acquisition Collector, vide award dated 16.12.2008, offered market price at the rates .
varying from Rs. 1,693.44 per Biswa to Rs. 247.35/-
per Biswa depending on the nature of the land.
4. Claimants filed reference petition, under Section 18 of the Act, seeking enhancement of amount of compensation.
Learned District Judge, Shimla, vide impugned award reference r by to dated 28.08.2015, answered enhancing the compensation the @ Rs. 10,000/- per Biswa.

5. Aggrieved against the impugned award dated 28.08.2015, passed by learned District Judge,
Shimla, H.P., in Land Reference No. 20-S/14 of 2013, RFA No. 446 of 2015, has been filed by the claimants, on the ground that the compensation awarded to them is on lesser side, whereas the State of Himachal Pradesh has assailed the same award in RFA No. 350 of 2016, on the ground that the enhancement given by learned Reference Court in respect of the market value of acquired land is without any basis.

6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have also gone through the record of the case .
carefully.

7. Sh. G.D. Verma, learned Senior Counsel, has contended that the learned Reference Court had erred in not assessing the market value of the acquired land in parity with the market value awarded Sukh Ram (Deceased) Through Lrs vs State Of Himachal Pradesh And Ors on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120478580/
2 by the Land Acquisition Collector for the land acquired Thekra for the purpose of construction of a road.
r in village
According to him, in both the cases the basis for assessment of market value was taken to be the value as existed in village Nerwa.

Whereas village Thekra was at a distance of about 12 Kms from Nerwa, village Diyandli was adjacent to village Nerwa and for such reason, the claimants in the instant case were entitled to compensation for their land in village Diyandli at least at par with the rate of market value assessed for village Thekra.
8. No doubt, claimants have been able to prove that village Diyandli was nearer to village Nerwa as compared to village Thekra.

The claimants have placed on record a site map prepared by Patwari (Ext. PW2/A), which also reflects the geographical position of .
villages Diyandli, Nerwa and Thekra.
However, this fact alone is not sufficient to accede to the arguments of learned Senior Counsel appearing for the claimants.

It is evident from award Ext. P-2, passed by Land Acquisition Collector in respect of acquisition of land in village Thekra that it was for a different road and the notification under Section 4 of the Act,
had been issued on 23.05.2008 i.e. almost after three years from the date of issuance of notification for acquisition of land of claimants.
It is trite that the compensation under the Act is awarded on the basis of market value of acquired land at the time of issuance of notification under Section 4 of the Act.

In view of the difference of about three years in the dates of issuance of notification in above referred two cases, the claimants are not right in seeking parity with the market value assessed for acquisition of land in village Thekra.

9. Further, no evidence has been led by the claimants before learned Reference Court to prove the market value of the land either in village Diyandli or Nerwa at the time of issuance of notification under .
Section 4 of the Act i.e. 21.07.2005.
There also is no evidence to suggest that there was no change as far as development is concerned between 2005 and 2008 in the areas, more particularly, in village Thekra or village Nerwa.

In absence of such evidence, learned Reference Court had ventured into an exercise on probabilities and had enhanced the market value of the land of the claimants to Rs.
10,000/- per Biswa, which cannot be said to be unreasonable for the reasons, firstly, that the claimants had not led any positive evidence and secondly, the State of Himachal Pradesh had also not been able to dispel the reasons for such a huge disparity of market value of the lands situated in village Diyandli and village Thekra, though, the gap between two acquisitions was of about three years.
10. The view taken by learned Reference Court is the probable and reasonable view and cannot be said to be perverse keeping in view all the attending facts and circumstances of the case.

In result, both these appeals fail.

The award dated 28.08.2015, passed by learned District Judge, .
Shimla, H.P., in Land Reference No. 20-S/14 of 2013, is upheld and affirmed.
12. These appeals, are accordingly disposed of, so also the pending miscellaneous application(s), if any.

14th March, 2024  (sushma)
